2	
3	> Build context governance for long-running local coding agents.
4	
5	ECC Curator will evolve incrementally, validating the governance model before introducing advanced optimization and decision intelligence. The primary workload is long-running autonomous coding sessions under finite context and hardware budgets. Token reduction is an efficiency measure, not a success criterion by itself; task completion and quality must be evaluated alongside it.
6	
7	Implementation specs: [Governor Algorithm](GOVERNOR_ALGORITHM.md), [Scoring Spec](SCORING_SPEC.md), [Inventory API](INVENTORY_API.md), and [Prompt Assembler](PROMPT_ASSEMBLER.md).
8	
9	## Current status
10	
11	The deterministic inventory, rules, scoring, Governor, and prompt-assembly pipeline for Phases 1–2 is implemented. Its integration with Claude Code is limited and experimental: an opt-in `UserPromptSubmit` hook adds explicitly selected governed context, and a paired evaluation harness is available. This does not govern the full conversation or autonomous tool turns, and no benchmark results or outcome improvements have been established.
12	
13	**Current focus:** validate the Phase 1–2 pipeline in bounded, repeatable baseline-versus-governed workloads using the Phase 5 evaluation tooling. The evaluation harness exists, but the benchmark datasets, repeated agent runs, and resource measurements listed in Phase 5 remain future work. Do not treat Phase 7 as complete based on the experimental Claude Code hook.

8	
9	This document defines the evaluation strategy, benchmarks, datasets, and success criteria used throughout the project.

12	
13	The first evaluation profile should reflect long-running local coding sessions rather than isolated prompt compression:

18	| Models | ISTA-DASLab/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GSQ-RCO-Coder-GGUF; future local coding models |
19	| Hardware profile | 32 GB RAM, 16 GB VRAM |
20	| Context windows | 64K and 128K tokens |

1	# Context Model
2	
3	> Context is not a conversation history.
4	>
5	> Context is a portfolio of information competing for limited attention.
6	
7	ECC Curator models context accumulated during long-running coding sessions as structured items competing for inclusion within a finite token budget. This is the intended model; it does not imply an implemented runtime.
8	
9	This document defines the core context abstractions used throughout the system.
10	
11	Implementation details for inventory operations, scoring, governance, and assembly are specified in [Inventory API](INVENTORY_API.md), [Scoring Spec](SCORING_SPEC.md), [Governor Algorithm](GOVERNOR_ALGORITHM.md), and [Prompt Assembler](PROMPT_ASSEMBLER.md).
12

14	
15	# Design Goals
16	
17	The context model must be:
18	
19	- Token-aware
20	- Model-agnostic
21	- Explainable
22	- Extensible
23	- Optimisable
24	- Deterministic
25	
26	Most importantly, Context items must be evaluated according to their task relevance and budget cost, not assumed to be equally valuable.

36	    ├── Context Item

38	```
39

+ # Context Classifier

> Experimental and deliberately narrow. It classifies from explicit metadata
> only; it does not inspect content, use an LLM, or contact any external
> service. Classification is a convenience in front of the existing inventory
> ingestion contract, not a replacement for callers supplying a type.

The classifier is the Phase 1 deliverable behind `src/classify/classify.ts`
(contracts in `src/types/classifier.ts`, tested in `tests/classifier.test.ts`).
It answers one question — "what context type should this item carry?" — from
explicit signals, and refuses to answer when the signals do not support one.

## Inputs and signals

`classifyContext` takes a `ContextClassificationInput`:

- `explicitType` (optional) — caller-provided type. When present it always
  wins: it is honoured even if it is an extension outside the known vocabulary
  (`knownType: false` records that), and conflicting signals never rewrite it.
- `source` (required) — normalized: trimmed, lowercased, hyphens folded to
  underscores, then split on whitespace/commas/semicolons into tokens.
- `tags` (optional) — normalized to trim + lowercase + hyphen fold; tags match
  the vocabulary by exact text, they are not token-split.

Content is never inspected: the classifier cannot and does not guess from
content. Anything not in the signal vocabulary matches nothing.
